headline: Tabled first reading of policies DJ and DJH on bidding and purchasing; accepted one resignation, two nominations, and four retirements.
summary: The meeting covered staffing changes, a remote learning update, and two purchasing policies. Members accepted one resignation, two nominations, and four retirements. The purchasing policies were tabled until the next meeting.
decisions: Approved the resignation of Rachel Davis, pre-K assistant at JFK, with 7 yes votes.
Approved the nomination of an individual as a day-to-day permanent substitute at Biddeford Primary School, with 7 yes votes.
Approved the nomination of Hannah Larochelle as physical education teacher at JFK and BPS, with 7 yes votes.
Accepted with regret the retirement of Cindy Bato, educational technician at BHS, with 34 years of service, with 7 yes votes.
Accepted with regret the retirement of John Bedard, custodian at BHS, with 20 years of service, with 7 yes votes.
Accepted with regret the retirement of Robert St. Cyr, custodian at BMS, with 12 years of service, with 7 yes votes.
Accepted with regret the retirement of Cynthia Taylor, van driver at the transportation department, with 25 years of service, with 7 yes votes.
Tabled the first reading of policies DJ (bidding and purchasing) and DJH (purchasing and contracting staff code of conduct) until the next meeting.
discussion: Remote learning update: Staff from the primary, intermediate, middle, high school, and technology center described how remote and hybrid learning works in each building. Members asked about attendance and live teaching time.
Attendance tracking: Staff said attendance forms give daily data, but some students may be doing the work without completing the form. Staff said they are still studying the data.

Recording live lessons: Members asked whether remote and in-person lessons could be recorded for students who miss class. Staff cited student privacy and FERPA, along with limits on video storage and bandwidth.
